A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable 26-page CASPER study, including Appendices A–H. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and acknowledgments page.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier evaluations and empirical analyses of human-written and LLM-generated stories, including Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classifier evaluations, story-corpus analyses, and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: The eight-category-pair CASPER classifier, Llama-70B judge, separate classification calls, and selected prompting templates are unchanged (Section 3; Appendix B.1).

E1.justification: Both versions analyze English short-story protagonists using the same human-story sources and generated-story corpus across the same four genres. No task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 3 compares the same prompting variants, and Table 4 retains the same Llama-70B versus GPT4o-mini comparison. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 100-story annotated test set, model configurations, macro-F1 evaluation, and generation settings remain identical, including temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.9 for open-source models.

E4.justification: The classifier-error analyses, creative-prompt control, source-comparability experiment, and additional genre and repeated-generation analyses are unchanged (Appendices B.3, D, E, and H).

E5.justification: Both retain the same three-run reporting and bootstrap significance statement in Table 3, inter-rater statistics in Appendix B, and standard-deviation error bars in Figures 3–5.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 4 retains closure macro-F1 scores of 75.12% for Llama-70B and 39.27% for GPT4o-mini; the appendix results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The eight-component task formulation in Section 3.2 and majority-label representation in RQ1 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a character-portrayal classifier, a curated story corpus, and comparisons of human-written and LLM-generated characters.

C2.justification: The interpretations and takeaways remain identical, as do limitations concerning English creative stories, possible AI contamination of human-written stories, classifier errors, and applicability beyond narratives.

D1.justification: Prompts, model identifiers, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime, data-processing details, and code/data access disclosures are unchanged. The funding addition supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and novelty positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic text reflows on page 9 without adding or removing references.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments add NSF grant IIS2047232 and adjust existing grant-number formatting. The first-page arXiv version/date stamp is updated; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment causes localized changes to line breaks and reference placement on page 9, and the first-page margin stamp changes. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 expands funding credit and updates version metadata, producing only localized reflow. Methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical, so these administrative edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
